questions.question: What is the most important mental model for an lxml XPath query?
options: It scans the original byte string without parsing
It runs against the tree produced under the selected parser policy
It executes page JavaScript before selecting elements
It always ignores XML namespaces
questions.explanation: lxml queries the parsed tree. Parser format, recovery, namespaces, and validation can all affect the nodes available to the expression.

questions.question: When does iterparse() provide a bounded-memory design?
options: Whenever the function is called, with no application cleanup
Only when every event is a start event
When completed records can be emitted and no-longer-needed subtrees and preceding siblings are cleared
When huge_tree=True is enabled
questions.explanation: iterparse emits events while building a tree. The application must process complete elements and release tree references that future work no longer needs.

questions.question: An XML document declares xmlns="urn:orders". Why does //order return no elements?
options: XPath cannot query XML
The elements have the expanded name {urn:orders}order and XPath needs a bound prefix
The document must be parsed as HTML
The order elements must have IDs
questions.explanation: XPath has no default element namespace. Bind a prefix such as o to urn:orders and query //o:order.

questions.question: A partner document is well-formed XML but quantity="unknown" violates the agreed XSD integer type. Which statement is correct?
options: Well-formedness proves the partner contract is valid
HTML recovery should repair the quantity
XML Schema validation can reject the document even though XML syntax is well-formed
huge_tree=True will validate the type
questions.explanation: Parsing checks XML syntax; schema validation checks the additional structural and typed contract. They are separate decisions.

questions.question: Why is huge_tree=True inappropriate for an untrusted XML upload?
options: It disables parser security restrictions for very deep trees and long text
It forces every document to use HTML semantics
It automatically downloads external schemas
It prevents XPath compilation
questions.explanation: The option expands the parser's accepted resource envelope by disabling protections. Untrusted input should remain bounded by parser and external limits.

questions.question: Why compile etree.XPath when the same query shape runs repeatedly?
options: To execute JavaScript embedded in XML
To compile the expression once and bind changing values as variables
To make namespaces unnecessary
To turn malformed HTML into XML
questions.explanation: A compiled XPath object can be reused, and variable binding keeps application values separate from expression text.

questions.question: Which production boundary belongs outside lxml?
options: Binding namespace prefixes for XPath
Compiling an XML Schema validator
Enforcing HTTP timeouts, response-byte limits, and access authorization
Clearing completed iterparse elements
questions.explanation: lxml parses supplied input. Acquisition policy, authorization, transport limits, and remote execution belong to the surrounding I/O layer.
